title: Morning Intel
bullets: Markets: US stocks fell Monday and futures point lower again Tuesday as AI-slowdown fears deepen a chip-stock selloff (Nvidia, Intel down sharply on reports TSMC asked suppliers to delay high-end chipmaking equipment shipments); cybersecurity names (CrowdStrike, Palo Alto Networks, Fortinet) rallied 9-14% on the AI-safety story.
Markets: The 10-year Treasury yield briefly topped 5% for the first time since 2023 on inflation worries tied to surging oil, before easing back to roughly 4.96-5.0%.
Markets: Brent crude climbed to ~$107-108/bbl (WTI ~$103) after Saudi Arabia shut its East-West pipeline, the key Strait-of-Hormuz bypass, following drone attacks; repairs could take months.

Companies: OpenAI's Sam Altman confirmed the company won't IPO in 2026, calling it an 'ill-advised moment' given AI-safety concerns and pushing the target to 2027; Anthropic is still reportedly on track for a possible IPO by year-end near a $2.3T valuation.

Companies: AI leaders (Anthropic's Amodei, OpenAI's Altman, Elon Musk) called for 'pacing' AI development; Trump publicly dismissed the warnings ('whoever wins AI wins'), while Microsoft published a 'Humanist AI' code pledging models stay under human control.

Macro/Policy: The Fed's FOMC meets today and Wednesday, with the rate decision a near coin-flip between a hold and a 25bp hike under new Chair Kevin Warsh, who says there's still 'work to do' on inflation.
Macro/Policy: Saudi Arabia blamed drones launched from Iraq for the pipeline attack; the IEA cut its 2026 global oil demand forecast by 2.5M bpd as Hormuz-linked disruptions drag on.
